newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 16.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Meetings on both sides of the farmers' blockades appear to show light at the end of the tunnel. Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas is to ask for compensation for farmers at today's agriculture ministers meeting in Brussels.
--Tax officials have called off their 24-hour strike for tomorrow following the government's satisfaction of their demands.

--A new ICAP poll shows a 28.5 percent of Greeks believe a moratorium on flyovers over Cyprus would show the international community Greece's good will for a mutually acceptable solution to the Cyprus issue. However, 23.9 say it would show that Greece was bowing to pressure from Turkey and the US and 24.2 say it would encourage Turkey to make further demands. 50.2 percent say the government should give top priority to effectively dealing with the Turkish threat.

--Alternate Foreign Minister George Papandreou and Turkey's Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller put their cards on the table at a dinner for EU foreign ministers in Dublin on Saturday night. Ciller reiterated Ankara's demands for EU funds and dialogue with Greece, with Papandreou responding that Greece wanted to see Turkey take the Imia islets dispute to the Hague.
--Leading ruling party PASOK member Theodoros Tsoukatos says that the blockades are daily thinning and that they are now playing a purely political role.

--Teachers begin a 48-hour strike today and will continue labour action into the new year. On the farmers' front, Prime Minister Costas Simitis says there is support for Greece at today's agriculture council.
--The City of Athens yesterday unveiled the tallest Christmas tree in Europe, smack in the middle of Syntagma Square. The 31.5 metre tree is lit up by 50,000 lights.
--Tomorrow sees the beginning of a barrage of strikes while farmers will decide today whether they will drive down to Athens on Wednesday. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
